title: Emotion regulation and depressive course of illness – a reminder-based online reappraisal training
summary: The ability to influence the nature and intensity of our emotions (emotion regulation, ER) plays an important role in the development and maintenance of affective disorders such as depression (MDD). It is important not only to know different ER strategies, but also to be able to apply them flexibly, i.e., in a way that is appropriate to the current situation. However, it is not yet clear to what extent this flexibility can be influenced. Clinically, these ER-related skills are particularly relevant for individuals with negative childhood experiences. Therefore, in our study, we would like to conduct ER training (ERT) with 200 MDD patients, half of whom score above the cut-off value for negative childhood experiences (CTQ). Patients will be randomly assigned to either the experimental group (ERT) or the active control group (cognitive training) and will then undergo 2 weeks of intensive EMA, followed by 8 weeks of online training, followed by another 2 weeks of intensive EMA. An MRI scan will be performed at the beginning and end of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Major Depression diagnosis,
half of patients score suprathreshold on childhood maltreatment scale (CTQ)
Exclusion criteria:
manic episodes in present or past (= diagnosis of bipolar disorder), all MRI contraindications, substance use disorder, current medication with benzodiazepines, current participation in another intervention study from the SFB CRC 393
